why: A witness's args are the input as drawn, rendered before either side runs. addKey adds a key to its Map argument, deposit writes a field of its record argument, pushItem pushes onto its array argument; each candidate writes a different value, so lane B finds a WITNESS on the argument after the call, and the witness's args must show the argument before the parent's write. scaled writes nothing and its outcome changes: its args are the draw as well. sumBoth reads the length through a local and adds in the other order: proved. count is untouched.
